doc.title: IAD ATCT SOP
doc.summary: Dulles ATCT SOP (Version I): positions and frequencies, runway configurations, clearance delivery rules (altitudes, departure gates, destination altitude restrictions), ground/local/ramp duties, departure headings and fixes, releases and arrival procedures.

items.title: Purpose, audience, cancellation, changes
items.text: Order describes airspace structure, procedures and policy for controllers working an operational IAD position on VATSIM; applies to all vZDC controllers and visiting controllers training with vZDC. Available at vzdc.org/publications/downloads. Cancels the Washington Dulles ATCT SOP Version 1.51 (effective August 21, 2020). Changes are highlighted in grey.

items.title: Non-standard runway configurations
items.text: Established configurations in 2-2-2 to 2-2-7 are preferred. Local controller may use a non-standard configuration as weather and traffic permit so long as: (a) it does not negatively affect traffic flow, (b) it is deemed necessary due to weather and traffic, and (c) Potomac Consolidated TRACON (PCT) is aware of it.

items.title: North Operation: land 1L/1C/1R, depart 1C/1R
items.text: Runways 1L, 1C and 1R are primary arrival runways; 1C and 1R are primary departure runways. North and east departures should be assigned runway 1R; south and west departures runway 1C. Use only when sustained wind is greater than 15 knots from the north.

items.title: North with 30: depart 30 and 1R
items.text: Primary arrival runways printed as "1L, 1R, and 1R"; runways 30 and 1R are primary departure runways. All departures should be assigned runway 30 unless operational advantage can be gained using 1R. Runway 30 departures may not be cleared for takeoff if a runway 1C arrival is within 2.27nm of the threshold or a runway 1L arrival is within 3.56 NM of the threshold. Use when sustained wind is 15 knots or less from the north (text also says: only when greater than 15 knots from the south).

items.title: RWY 30 takeoff vs 1C/1L arrivals
items.text: In North with 30, runway 30 departures may not be cleared for takeoff if a runway 1C arrival is within 2.27nm of the threshold or a runway 1L arrival is within 3.56 NM of the threshold.
items.restr: No T/O if 1C arr within 2.27nm / 1L arr within 3.56 NM

items.title: South Operation: land 19L/19C/19R, depart 19C/19L
items.text: Runways 19L, 19C and 19R are primary arrival runways; 19C and 19L are primary departure runways. North and east departures should be assigned runway 19C; south and west departures runway 19L.

items.title: South with 30: depart 30 and 19L
items.text: Runways 19L, 19C and 19R are primary arrival runways; runways 30 and 19L are primary departure runways. All departures should be assigned runway 30 unless operational advantage can be gained using 19L. Use when sustained wind is 15 knots or less from the south.

items.title: South with 12: land 12, depart 19L/19C
items.text: Runway 12 is the primary arrival runway; 19L and 19C are primary departure runways. North and east departures should be assigned 19C; south and west departures 19L. Use only when sustained wind is greater than 20 knots and closely aligns with runway 12.
items.restr: Arr RWY 12; N/E deps 19C; S/W deps 19L

items.title: Landing 30: approach 1R, circle to 30
items.text: Runway 30 is the primary arrival and departure runway. PCT shall use an instrument approach for runway 1R and IAD local control shall issue circling instructions for runway 30. Use when sustained wind is greater than 25 knots and closely aligns with runway 30.

items.title: Routine runway configuration change
items.text: The CIC determines the need for active runway changes; in a routine change departures may depart the runway originally assigned. Steps: (1) give PCT the last departure's ID, estimated departure time and runway; (2) once it departs, ensure no other aircraft departs without a release from PCT (text prints "BWI"); (3) ensure departures off the new runway have the appropriate DP and departure frequency; (4) PCT informs the CIC when sector reconfiguration is complete; (5) ensure the ATIS is updated.

items.title: ASDE: transponders on in movement area
items.text: Ground Control and Local Control shall ensure all aircraft operating in a movement area have transponders on.

items.title: DC SFRA at IAD
items.text: DC SFRA is simulated on VATSIM with a modified procedure. VFR departures are expected to file a DC SFRA flight plan. The FRZ does not impose higher requirements, so normal VFR operations, including pattern work, shall be allowed if workload permits. Ref: VATSIM DC SFRA Procedures and Pilot Guide (vzdc.org/publications/downloads).
items.restr: VFR deps file SFRA flight plan

items.title: Clearance Delivery responsibilities
items.text: Clearance Delivery must (a) formulate and issue IFR and VFR clearances to aircraft departing IAD, and (b) review proposed flight plans, verify accuracy and amend routings and altitudes as necessary per the appropriate LOAs.

items.title: IFR clearance: SID, 3,000, expect cruise in 10
items.text: All IFR departures should be assigned a departure and transition consistent with their direction of flight. Aircraft unable to fly a SID shall be assigned the CPTAL1 Departure Procedure. All IFR departures shall be issued an initial altitude of 3,000 and to expect filed cruise altitude ten minutes after departure.

items.title: Non-SID aircraft: CPTAL1 departure
items.text: If an aircraft is unable to fly a SID, it shall be assigned the CPTAL1 Departure Procedure.

items.title: vTDLS PDCs for IFR
items.text: IAD is equipped with vTDLS to issue Pre-Departure Clearances (PDCs) to IFR aircraft.

items.title: VFR flight following flight plan requirements
items.text: VFR aircraft requesting flight following shall have in their VFR flight plan prior to departure: destination airport, aircraft type, and requested VFR altitude. VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern require a squawk code (no altitude restriction needed).

items.title: VFR departure (Turbojet): maintain VFR AOB 3,000
items.text: All VFR departures receive a class B clearance with a restriction to maintain VFR at or below 3,000 (Turbojet). VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern do not require an altitude restriction.

items.title: VFR departure (Propeller): maintain VFR AOB 2,500
items.text: All VFR departures receive a class B clearance with a restriction to maintain VFR at or below 2,500 (Propeller). VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern do not require an altitude restriction.

items.title: VFR departure (Helicopters): maintain VFR AOB 1,300
items.text: All VFR departures receive a class B clearance with a restriction to maintain VFR at or below 1,300 (Helicopters). VFR aircraft remaining in the pattern do not require an altitude restriction.

items.title: East/North departures: ASPER 125.050
items.text: Assign departure frequency per SID, departure gate or direction of flight: East/North departures get ASPER (125.050). See TBL 5-2-2 for the ASPER departure fixes.

items.title: South/West departures: TILLY 126.650
items.text: Assign departure frequency per SID, departure gate or direction of flight: South/West departures get TILLY (126.650). See TBL 5-2-2 for the TILLY departure fixes.

items.title: Departure exit gates required
items.text: PCT uses departure exit gates for IFR departures to destinations outside PCT airspace. Every IFR aircraft leaving IAD must leave PCT airspace bound for one of these gates, unless coordinated otherwise. High gates for aircraft filed above 10,000 feet; low gates at or below 10,000 feet. Prop and turboprop aircraft may be routed via a low altitude gate regardless of altitude; low altitude aircraft may receive vectors to join any low altitude airway.

items.title: Ground Control responsibilities
items.text: Ground Control must (a) sequence aircraft that have the same first fix or direction of departure with other aircraft, and (b) keep runway exits clear for landing aircraft.

items.title: Runway crossings: verbal coordination
items.text: Blanket crossings are not approved at IAD. Ground control must verbally coordinate with local control for any aircraft that requires a runway crossing.

items.title: With-30 configs: assign runway 30
items.text: When using North with 30 or South with 30, assign all departures runway 30. If operationally advantageous, aircraft may be assigned runway 1R/19L.

items.title: North Op: North/East bound departures RWY 1R
items.text: In North Operation, assign North/East bound departures runway 1R. Fixes listed are the ASPER (North/East) departure fixes from TBL 5-2-2. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control via verbal or nonverbal methods.

items.title: North Op: South/West bound departures RWY 1C
items.text: In North Operation, assign South/West bound departures runway 1C. Fixes listed are the TILLY (South/West) departure fixes from TBL 5-2-2. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control via verbal or nonverbal methods.

items.title: South Op: North/East bound departures RWY 19C
items.text: In South Operation, assign North/East bound departures runway 19C. Fixes listed are the ASPER (North/East) departure fixes from TBL 5-2-2. Assigning a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control via verbal or nonverbal methods.

items.title: South Op: South/West bound departures RWY 19L

items.title: Non-standard runway needs Local coordination
items.text: Assigning an aircraft a non-standard runway requires coordination with local control via verbal or nonverbal methods. A non-standard departure runway also requires Local Control to call PCT for release (5-2-3).

items.title: Ground East/North/West movement areas
items.text: Ground East, Ground North and Ground West are each responsible for the movement areas depicted in Appendix A.

items.title: Pushbacks: ramp control or pilot discretion
items.text: Ground control should not approve pushbacks; this falls under ramp control if online. If ramp control is not online, aircraft should be advised their pushback is at their discretion.

items.title: Local Control airspace AOB 2,000
items.text: Local Control assumes responsibility for the airspace depicted in Appendix B at or below 2,000 feet.

items.title: Local North: runway 1C/19C

items.title: Departure headings per TBL 5-2-1
items.text: All departures should be issued departure headings in accordance with table 5-2-1. Aircraft on the BUNZZ or RNLDI SID may be issued a heading if operational advantage will be gained.

items.title: BUNZZ / RNLDI SID: heading only if advantageous
items.text: Aircraft on the BUNZZ or RNLDI SID may be issued a heading if operational advantage will be gained.

items.title: North RWY 30 with SIMULS: 280-310 limits
items.text: Runways 1L, 1C, 1R and/or 30 in use: when departing RWY 30 and SIMULS are in use, turn no further west than 280 and no further northwest than 310.

items.title: South RWY 30 with SIMULS: 250-300 limits
items.text: Runways 19R, 19C, 19R and/or 30 in use (as printed): when departing RWY 30 and SIMULS are in use, turn no further northwest than 300 and no further southwest than 250.

items.title: LUAW authorized
items.text: LUAW procedures are authorized at IAD. Use LUAW when it is expected the aircraft will depart after conflicting traffic is clear of the runway/intersection; use good operating practices and memory aids. Landing clearances need not be withheld for traffic holding in position.

items.title: Blanket IFR releases and exceptions
items.text: IAD has blanket IFR releases unless: (a) a previous missed approach/go around occurred and PCT has not given back automatic releases; (b) PCT cancels automatic releases; or (c) an aircraft departs a non-standard departure runway. Then Local Control must call PCT for release stating ACID, runway and departure heading, and SID and transition or initial fix.
items.restr: Call for release if exception applies

items.title: Reduced separation 2.5 NM on final
items.text: Separation of IFR arrivals may be reduced to 2.5 NM within 10 NM of the runway on the final approach course, regardless of operation or runways in use, providing wake turbulence is not a factor.

items.title: Missed approach/go around: RWY HDG, 2,000
items.text: Local control shall immediately coordinate with PCT on a missed approach/go around. Unless otherwise coordinated, instruct the aircraft to fly runway heading and maintain 2,000 feet. Automatic releases are then suspended until released by PCT. Tower may re-sequence props if it ensures separation from all pertinent traffic and does not affect the sequence of other IFR arrivals sequenced by PCT.

items.title: Arrivals clear of runway to Ground
items.text: Once aircraft are clear of the runway, they shall be transferred to ground control unless otherwise coordinated.

items.title: Ramp Control area and authorization
items.text: Ramp Control is responsible for the non-movement area between taxiways Zulu and Juliet. It may be split as traffic requires or as permitted by the vZDC Events Coordinator, and shall only be used when approved by the Events Coordinator or a delegated Events Team member. When not utilized, Ground Control does not assume responsibility for Ramp Control.

items.title: Ramp Control duties: departures
items.text: Ramp Control shall: approve pushbacks and specify tail direction; issue runway assignments; provide Ground Control departure sequencing based on departure runway and gate; instruct aircraft to taxi via the appropriate taxiway, hold short of taxiway Zulu or Juliet and contact Ground Control. Ground Control may change runway assignments as necessary.

items.title: Ramp Control duties: arrivals
items.text: Ramp Control shall issue taxi instructions to aircraft entering the ramp from the movement areas, and transition aircraft taxiing across the ramp and transfer communications to the appropriate ground controller.

items.title: South Area Ramp: taxiways E and F
items.text: South Area Ramp (130.550) is responsible for taxiways E and F and their associated gates between taxiways J and Z.

items.title: North Area Ramp: taxiways A and B
items.text: North Area Ramp (119.125) is responsible for taxiways A and B and their associated gates between taxiways J and Z.

items.title: Midfield Area Ramp: taxiways C and D
items.text: Midfield Area Ramp (129.550) is responsible for taxiways C and D and their associated gates between taxiways J and Z.
